text:
Vegas arrives in Detroit on the third game of a four-game road trip and the third in four nights, riding a comeback: the Golden Knights trailed Pittsburgh in the third period on Tuesday and won 3-2 on Tomas Hertl's goal with 0:35 left. They're 2-1-2 in their last five and playing without Parker Wotherspoon. Detroit lost 4-2 at Tampa Bay in its last game and is without Dylan Larkin (suspended), Albert Johansson and Mason Appleton. In the four games since Larkin went out, Alex DeBrincat has taken his spot beside Lucas Raymond and Viktor Arvidsson, and Emmitt Finnie has moved onto the first power-play unit.

The teams look alike in open play, each with 53% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) at five on five. Our model has Vegas at 3.08 goals tonight and Detroit at 2.89. Detroit has been better than its results: a -2 goal difference against +5.2 expected, with finishing costing it about seven goals. The goalie matchup favors Vegas this year. Projected starter Carter Hart is at +0.12 goals saved above expected, which measures saves against the difficulty of the shots, while John Gibson sits at -6.3 after a +10.11 season last year.

Raymond, on a five-game point streak, is worth watching, and Arvidsson and DeBrincat each have a 35% chance to score on the power play's top unit. For Vegas, Mark Stone (35% to score) is our top pick, and Jack Eichel has the best chance of a multi-point night at 36%.
